title: Wrap-Up Check
description: Ten quick questions to lock in what you built today — takes about three minutes. The short form before it asks who you are so we can send you the trial link and follow up on anything you flagged in Lab 7. No score pressure: this is a recap, not an exam.

questions.prompt: You want to inspect the data mid-pipeline, after the filter but before anything is written. In PDI you...
options: Right-click the step and Preview — at any step, at any time
Add temporary logging code and re-deploy
Run the whole pipeline and query the target table
Export the stream to CSV and open it in Excel
questions.explanation: Preview works on every step while you build — the habit from Lab 1. You inspect the stream before anything is committed anywhere.

questions.prompt: How did the columns and types of the sales CSV get defined in your transformation?
options: Get Fields read the file and proposed the schema, which you could then correct
You wrote a schema file by hand first
PDI requires the source team to supply an XSD
Columns are always read as strings and cast later in SQL
questions.explanation: Get Fields infers names, types and formats from the data itself — and the grid lets you fix anything it guessed wrong. It's also why Lab 6 worked on a file PDI had never seen.

questions.prompt: In Lab 3 you brought together CSV sales, a JSON customer master, a product catalogue and a region reference. What staging was required first?
options: None — the streams were looked up and joined on the canvas as they flowed
All three files had to be loaded into MySQL first
The JSON had to be converted to CSV outside the tool
A schema registry entry for each source
questions.explanation: Stream lookup and Merge join both work on rows in flight — Stream lookup holds a small reference set in memory, Merge join streams two sorted inputs with full inner/outer semantics. Format differences disappear at the Input step; after that, everything is rows.

questions.prompt: After you changed customer C001's region and re-ran the load, the dimension table showed...
options: Two rows for C001 — the old region with its validity window closed, the new one open-ended
One updated row for C001 — the old region was overwritten
A constraint violation on the natural key
Twenty-one new rows — the whole file was reloaded
questions.explanation: That's a Type 2 slowly changing dimension: Dimension lookup/update versioned the changed record and left the other nineteen untouched — the behaviour that normally costs a page of hand-written MERGE SQL.
questions.source: Lab 4 — Track History with One Step

questions.prompt: In Lab 5, onboarding the fourth feed (the Scotland file) required...
options: Adding one row to control.csv — no pipeline was opened
Copying the template and editing its reader for the new file
A new transformation per feed, as usual
Regenerating the template from the driver
questions.explanation: Metadata injection turns pipeline configuration into data. The template stays untouched; the control file — which an operations team can own — defines the feeds.

questions.prompt: Which of these does moving from today's Developer Edition lab to a production deployment add? Select all that apply.
options: Scheduled, monitored execution on a server instead of a laptop designer
Clustered / scaled-out execution
A commercial licence covering production use, with support
A different pipeline format — today's transformations must be rebuilt
questions.explanation: Everything you built today is real PDI and moves to production as-is — what the platform adds is the operational layer (scheduling, monitoring, scale-out, governance) and the licence and support to run it in production.

questions.prompt: In Lab 2, what happened to the sales rows that failed validation?
options: They were routed down a reject stream and written to a file for the source team
The transformation stopped with an error on the first bad row
They were silently dropped
They were fixed automatically by the filter step
questions.explanation: Bad data is a routing decision, not a crash: the Filter rows FALSE branch carried the rejects to their own output, while the valid rows continued — visible on the canvas, no try/except code.

questions.prompt: Beyond the local files used today, where can PDI's Input steps read from?
options: Databases, Excel, cloud storage (S3), HTTP and other VFS locations — the same canvas pattern
Local CSV and text files only
Only sources that have a JDBC driver
Anything, but each source needs custom plugin development first
questions.explanation: The pattern you learned generalises: swap the Input step and the rest of the pipeline is unchanged — databases, spreadsheets, cloud object storage, APIs and message queues are all first-class sources.

questions.prompt: In production, what sequences your transformations, retries failures, and alerts someone when the source file doesn't arrive?
options: A job (.kjb), scheduled and monitored on a server
A cron script that calls each transformation in order
Each transformation schedules itself
The Filter rows step
questions.explanation: Jobs are the orchestration layer: success/failure routing between entries, retries, notifications — and a server runs them on schedule with logging and history.

questions.prompt: What does the Pentaho Developer Edition licence (BSL 1.1) cover?
options: Evaluation, development, and learning — production use requires a commercial licence
Any use, including production, free of charge
A 30-day time-limited trial that then stops working
Non-commercial personal use only
questions.explanation: Developer Edition is the full product for evaluating and building — it doesn't expire. Running it in production is what needs the commercial licence (which also brings support and certified updates).
